ICG in Liver Surgery, Ampullary Cancer Subtypes and a New Leak Stent
STITCHES Daily · Monday, 28 September 2026

Today, we cover fluorescence guidance in minimally invasive liver surgery, and genomic risk in ampullary cancer. We also examine how hospital organization affects evidence-based care, and review endoscopic treatment for cystic duct remnant stones and postoperative gastrointestinal leaks.

Papers in this episode:
1. Indocyanine Green Imaging in Minimally Invasive Liver Surgery
   Han et al., Tianjin Medical University, Tianjin, China — Surgical Endoscopy
   https://doi.org/10.1007/s00464-026-13265-8
2. Recurrence Patterns in Resected Ampullary Adenocarcinoma
   Ecker et al., Northwestern University, Chicago, IL, USA — Annals of Surgical Oncology
   https://doi.org/10.1245/s10434-026-20537-z
3. Centralized Cancer Care Yields Better Evidence Alignment
   Broman et al., University of Alabama at Birmingham, Birmingham, AL, USA — Journal of the American College of Surgeons
   https://doi.org/10.1097/XCS.0000000000002210
4. Endoscopic Approach for Cystic Duct Remnant Stones Effective
   Arif et al., University of California, Los Angeles, California, USA — Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
   https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gie.2026.08.008
5. Novel VAC-Stent Effective for Treating Post-Surgical GI Leaks
   Zito et al., A.O.R.N. Antonio Cardarelli, Naples — Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
   https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gie.2026.09.021
